ui.chooseLanguage: Which language do you want to use for Visual Slash?
ui.chooseLanguageSub: You can change it anytime with the 🌐 button. Your choice is saved only on this device.
ui.tagline: Tell AI what you want to get.
ui.heroP: You do not need to know prompting. Choose what you want — an image, document, data analysis, presentation, text or code — and Visual Slash helps you build clear instructions for AI.
ui.guideTitle: Visual Slash does not create the result: it prepares the instructions.
ui.guideLead: Build a natural-language prompt here, then copy it into your AI. You can use it for images, documents, data analysis, presentations, text and code, when the AI you choose supports that task.
ui.note: Capabilities depend on the AI you use. Visual Slash is independent and is not affiliated with or sponsored by AI providers.
ui.what: What do you want to get?
ui.whatSub: Choose a category. You do not need to know technical terms.
ui.dontKnow: I do not know what to choose
ui.advisor: Write what you want in your own words below. Visual Slash suggests a starting combination without external services.
ui.subject: WHAT DO YOU WANT TO CREATE?
ui.about: An independent open-source assistant for building clear, reusable prompts. It helps you request images, documents, analyses, presentations, text and code without knowing prompting terminology. Available capabilities depend on the AI where you paste the prompt.
ui.finalCheck: Before finalizing, verify that the result matches the goal and do not invent missing information.
ui.chooseOptions: Choose the options above to define the result.
ui.whyIntro: Now choose type, style/content and delivery format.
ui.writeFirst: First write what you want to get, even in a simple sentence.
ui.prepared: I prepared a starting combination that you can change.
ui.recipeHint: Automatically fills a useful starting combination.
ui.categoryChange: The choices below change according to this category.

image: Photos, infographics, posters, drawings and image edits.
document: Reports, proposals, manuals, letters and structured documents.
data: Comparisons, tables, summaries, charts and spreadsheets.
presentation: Slides, pitches, commercial decks and training.
text: Emails, posts, articles, rewrites and summaries.
code: PWAs, HTML, JavaScript, Python, debugging and documentation.

image: What kind of image do you want?
Where or why will you use it?
document: What document do you want to create?
How do you want to receive it?
data: What should be done with the data?
How do you want to understand the results?
How should the data be handled?
How do you want to receive the work?
presentation: How do you want to receive it?
text: What should be preserved or checked?
How do you want the text?
code: How should the code be built?
